Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verse 1:

(p-14) Surah "al-Ahzab" (The Confederates)

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Ubayy ibn Ka'b (may Allah be pleased with him) said to Zirr: "How many verses do you count in Surah al-Ahzab?" He replied: "Seventy-three." Ubayy said: "By He in Whose hand is Ubayy's soul, it was equal to Surah al-Baqarah, or longer. We recited from it the verse of stoning: ﴿The elderly man and the elderly woman, if they commit adultery, stone them absolutely as a punishment from Allah, and Allah is Mighty and Wise﴾." Ubayy meant that this was among what was abrogated (nasakh, abrogation: the cancelling of a ruling or recitation by later revelation) from the Qur'an. As for what is related, that this addition was in a written sheet in the house of 'Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) and the domestic animal (dajin, a tame animal such as a goat or sheep) ate it, that is among the fabrications of the heretics (malahida) and the Rafidah (Rafidites).

﴿O Prophet⦈, with a hamza according to Nafi', meaning: "O one who is informed by Us, trusted with Our secrets, conveying Our address to Our beloved ones." He did not say "O Muhammad" as He said "O Adam" and "O Musa", out of honour for him and to elevate his merit, and He stated his name in His words ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah﴾ [al-Fath: 29] and similar verses, to teach people that he is the Messenger of Allah.

﴿Fear Allah﴾: remain upon the fear of Allah, persist in it, and increase in it, for it is a gate whose reach cannot be attained. ﴿And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites﴾: do not assist them in anything, and be wary of them, for they are the enemies of Allah and of the believers. (p-15) It is narrated that "Abu Sufyan, 'Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, and Abu al-A'war al-Sulami came to Medina after the battle of Uhud and lodged with 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy. The Prophet granted them safe conduct on condition that they speak with him. They said: 'Renounce mention of our gods, and say that they benefit and intercede.' The hypocrites backed them in this, and the Muslims resolved to kill them, whereupon this verse was revealed." That is: "Fear Allah regarding breaking the covenant, and do not obey the disbelievers from the people of Mecca or the hypocrites from the people of Medina in what they demanded."

﴿Indeed Allah is ever Knowing⦈ of the wickedness of their deeds,

﴿Wise⦈ in delaying the command to fight them.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verse 2:

﴿And follow what is revealed to you from your Lord﴾, in steadfastness upon piety and in abandoning obedience to the disbelievers and the hypocrites,

﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, who reveals to you,

﴿is ever, of what you do, Acquainted﴾; i.e., He has never ceased to be Knowing of your deeds. It was said: the reason He used the plural is that the intended meaning of His words "follow" (ittabi') is he (the Prophet) and his companions. And with the letter ya' (yaʿmalūna, "they do"), Abu ʿAmr (read it): i.e., of what the disbelievers and the hypocrites do of their scheming against you and their plotting against you.

**﴿And put your trust in God﴾**: rely on Him with your affair and entrust it to His management.

**﴿And God is sufficient as a Guardian﴾**: a Preserver, to whom every matter is entrusted. Al-Zajjaj said: Although its wording is that of a statement of fact, its meaning is: "Be content with God as your Guardian."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verse 4:

﴿Allah has not made for any man two hearts within his body, nor has He made your wives whom you divorce by zihar (ẓihār) into your mothers, nor has He made your adopted sons (ad'iyā') into your sons.﴾ That is: Allah has not joined two hearts in one body, nor marriage and motherhood in one woman, nor sonship and adoption in one man. The meaning is that just as He (exalted is He) has not given a person two hearts, because one of two things must hold: either he acts with the other heart in one of the acts of the heart, in which case one of them is superfluous and not needed; or he acts with this one differently from how he acts with that one, and that leads to the whole being described as both willing and unwilling, knowing and suspecting, certain and doubting, in one and the same state. Likewise, He has not allowed one woman to be both a mother and a wife to the same man, because the mother is served and the wife serves, and between them there is incompatibility. Nor may one man be both an adopted son (da'iyy) of a man and his son, because sonship is an essential attachment by lineage, whereas adoption is an accidental attachment by naming only, and nothing more. Nor can one thing be both genuine and not genuine at once. This is an example which Allah (exalted is He) gave concerning Zayd ibn Ḥārithah, a man of the tribe of Kalb, who was taken captive as a child. Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām bought him for his paternal aunt Khadījah. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married her, she gave him to him. His father and uncle then sought him, and he was given the choice, but he chose the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He freed him and adopted him, and they used to say: "Zayd ibn Muḥammad." When the Prophet ﷺ married Zaynab, who had been married to Zayd, the hypocrites said: "Muḥammad has married the wife of his son, while he forbids it." Then Allah revealed this verse. It is also said: the hypocrites used to say: "Muḥammad has two hearts, one with you and one with his companions." It is also said: Abū Ma'mar was the most retentive of the Arabs, so he was called "the one with two hearts," and Allah refuted their saying and gave him as an example concerning ẓihār and adoption.

The indefiniteness in "rajul" (a man), the insertion of "min" (of) which is for totality (istighrāq) before "qalbayn" (two hearts), and the mention of "al-jawf" (the body) are for emphasis. "Al-lā'ī" (with a yāʾ after the hamza), wherever it occurs, is read by the Kufans and the Syrians as "allā'ī"; "al-lā'" is read by Nāfi', Ya'qūb and Sahl. It is the plural of "allatī" (who). "Tuẓāhirūna" (you divorce by ẓihār) is read by 'Āṣim, from "ẓāhara," when a man says to his wife: "You are to me like the back of my mother." "Taẓāharūna" is read by ʿAlī, Ḥamzah and Khalaf. "Taẓẓāharūna" is read by the Syrians, from "iẓẓāhara," with the meaning of "taẓāhara." Others read "taẓẓahharūna," from "iẓẓahhara," with the meaning of "taẓahhara." It takes "min" because it includes the meaning of distance, since it was a form of divorce in the pre-Islamic period. Its parallel is "ālā min imra'atihi" (he swore off from his wife): when it is given the meaning of separation, it takes "min." Otherwise "ālā," in its basic sense, which is the meaning of "ḥalafa" and "aqsama" (to swear), does not carry this ruling.

"Al-da'iyy" is of the pattern "fa'īl" in the sense of "maf'ūl" (passive), and is one who is claimed as a son. Its plural is irregularly "af'iyā'," because its usual pattern is for those words that carry the sense of "fā'il," such as "taqiyy" and "atqiyā'," and "shaqiyy" and "ashqiyā'." This does not apply to words like "ramiyy" and "samiyy," owing to verbal similarity.

﴿That is your saying with your mouths.﴾ That is: your saying to a wife, "She is my mother," and to an adopted son, "He is my son," is a saying which you utter with your tongues, and it has no reality, since a son is by birth, and likewise a mother.

﴿And Allah speaks the truth﴾ That is: what is truly apparent and inward.

﴿And He guides to the way﴾ That is: (p-١٧) the way of truth. Then He stated what the truth is, and guided to what is the way of truth, which is His saying:

﴿Call them by [the names of] their fathers; that is more just⦆ — ﴿aqsat﴾ means ﴿a'dal﴾, more just — ﴿in the sight of Allah﴾. He showed that calling them by their fathers' names is the more fitting of the two options with regard to justice and fairness. It was said: in the Jahiliyya (the pre-Islamic "age of ignorance"), if a man was impressed by another man's child, he would take him into his own household, give him a share equal to that of a male among his own children in the inheritance, and he would be attributed to him, so it would be said, "So-and-so son of So-and-so." Then observe the eloquence of this speech: it joined the imperative clauses (al-jumal al-talabiyya), then separated the declarative clauses (al-khabariyya) from them and joined them to one another, then separated the nominal clauses (al-ismiyya) from them and joined them to one another, then separated [the sentence] with an imperative clause.

﴿But if you do not know their fathers﴾, meaning: if you do not know that they have fathers whom you can attribute them to,

﴿then they are your brothers in religion and your protégés﴾. That is: then they are your brothers in religion and your allies in religion. They used to say, "This is my brother," and "This is my mawla (protégé/client)," and "O my brother," and "O my mawla," intending brotherhood in religion and the bond of allegiance in it.

﴿And there is no blame upon you for what you have done in error﴾, meaning: there is no sin upon you for what you did of that in error, being ignorant, before the prohibition had come down.

﴿But what your hearts intended [is blameworthy]﴾. The sin lies upon you for what you did deliberately after the prohibition; or, there is no sin upon you if you say to the child of another, "O my son," by way of mistake and a slip of the tongue, but [there is sin] if you say it deliberately. Here "mā" is in the genitive position, conjoined to the first "mā." It is also permissible that what is meant is pardon for error, not for deliberate action, in a general sense. Then, through its generality, it encompasses both the error of adoption (al-tabanni, adoption) and its deliberate practice. When adoption occurs: if the adopted person is of unknown lineage and younger than the adopter, his lineage is established from him and he is freed if he was the adopter's slave. If he is older than the adopter, lineage is not established and he is freed, according to Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him. As for one whose lineage is known, his lineage is not established through adoption, and he is freed if he was a slave.

﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾, who will not hold you to account for error, and who accepts repentance from the one who acts deliberately.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (*Madarik al-Tanzil*) on surah 33, verse 6:

﴿The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves.﴾ That is: he has more right over them in every matter of the religion and of the worldly life, and his judgment is more binding upon them than their own judgment. So it is incumbent upon them to give up their own lives rather than his, and to make them a ransom for him. Or it means: he is more compassionate (*ar'af*) toward them, more tender (*a'taf*) toward them, and more beneficial (*anfa'*) to them, like His saying: ﴿He is kind and merciful to the believers.﴾ [al-Tawbah: 128]. In the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud: "The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves, and he is a father to them." Mujahid said: "Every prophet is the father of his community." For this reason the believers became brothers, because the Prophet ﷺ is their father in the religion.

﴿And his wives are their mothers.﴾ In the prohibition of marrying them and the obligation to honor them. Apart from that, they are like non-relatives in matters such as inheritance and the like. For this reason the prohibition did not extend to their daughters.

﴿And those of blood relationship⁠ ⁠﴾ — that is, kinsfolk and relatives —

﴿are closer to one another⁠ ⁠﴾ in inheritance. In the early period of Islam, Muslims used to inherit from one another by the bond of allegiance (*wilaya*) in religion and by emigration (*hijra*, migration), not by kinship. Then this was abrogated (*nusikha*, i.e., naskh, abrogation), and inheritance was made to be by the right of kinship.

﴿in the Book of Allah⁠ ⁠﴾ — in His ruling and decree; or in the Preserved Tablet (*al-Lawh al-Mahfuz*); or in what Allah has ordained.

﴿among the believers and the emigrants⁠ ⁠﴾ — it is permissible that this be an explanation of "those of blood relationship," meaning: the relatives among these people are more entitled to inherit from one another than outsiders. It may also be for the beginning of the end (*li-ibtida' al-ghaya*, i.e., indicating the starting point), meaning: "Those of blood relationship, by the right of kinship, are more entitled to inheritance than the believers," that is, "the Ansar (the Helpers), by the right of allegiance in religion, over the Muhajirun (the Emigrants), by the right of emigration."

﴿Except that you do a kindness to your allies⁠ ⁠﴾ — the exception is discontinuous (*istithna' min khilaf al-jins*, an exception of a different kind), meaning: "Yet your doing a kindness to your allies is permissible, and it is that you bequeath something to whomever you love from these people; this will be by bequest, not by inheritance." The verb *tafʿalu* (you do) is transitive with *ilá* (to) because it carries the meaning of *tusdū* (you extend/confer). The intended meaning of "allies" (*awliya'*) is the believers and the emigrants, by the bond of allegiance in religion.

﴿That was written in the Book as something inscribed⁠ ⁠﴾ — that is, the inheritance by blood ties was inscribed in the Tablet.

﴿And [mention] when We took from the prophets their covenant﴾: mention when We took from the prophets their covenant to convey the message and to call people to the upright religion,

﴿and [especially] from you﴾, specifically. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is placed before Noah and those after him, because this conjunction serves to show the excellence of these prophets, since they are the Ulu al-'Azm (the possessors of resolve) and the bearers of sacred laws (shara'i'). Since Muhammad (ﷺ) was the best of them, he was placed before them. Had it not been so, the one who came earlier in time would have been placed first,

﴿and from Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus son of Mary. And We took from them a solemn covenant﴾, (p-19) a firm one. He repeated the mention of the covenant because the attribute was joined to it. And this is what we did,

﴿لِيَسْألَ﴾، اَللَّهُ،

﴿الصادِقِينَ﴾ أيْ: اَلْأنْبِياءَ،

﴿عَنْ صِدْقِهِمْ﴾، عَمّا قالُوهُ لِقَوْمِهِمْ، أوْ: لِيَسْألَ المُصَدِّقِينَ لِلْأنْبِياءِ عَنْ تَصْدِيقِهِمْ، لِأنَّ مَن قالَ لِلصّادِقِ: "صَدَقْتَ"، كانَ صادِقًا في قَوْلِهِ، أوْ: لِيَسْألَ الأنْبِياءَ ما الَّذِي أجابَتْهم أُمَمُهُمْ، وهو كَقَوْلِهِ: ﴿يَوْمَ يَجْمَعُ اللهُ الرُسُلَ فَيَقُولُ ماذا أُجِبْتُمْ﴾ [المائدة: ١٠٩]

﴿وَأعَدَّ لِلْكافِرِينَ﴾، بِالرُسُلِ،

﴿عَذابًا ألِيمًا﴾، وهو عَطْفٌ عَلى "أخَذْنا"، لِأنَّ المَعْنى أنَّ اللهَ أكَّدَ عَلى الأنْبِياءِ الدَعْوَةَ إلى دِينِهِ، لِأجْلِ إثابَةِ المُؤْمِنِينَ، وأعَدَّ لِلْكافِرِينَ عَذابًا ألِيمًا، أوْ عَلى ما دَلَّ عَلَيْهِ "لِيَسْألَ الصادِقِينَ"، كَأنَّهُ قالَ: "فَأثابَ المُؤْمِنِينَ، وأعَدَّ لِلْكافِرِينَ... ".

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verse 9:

﴿O you who have believed, remember the favor of Allah upon you﴾ i.e., what Allah bestowed upon you on the Day of the Confederates (al-Ahzab), which is the Day of the Trench (al-Khandaq), and it was one year after the battle of Uhud,

﴿when there came to you soldiers﴾ i.e., the confederates (al-Ahzab), namely Quraysh, Ghatafan, Qurayzah, and al-Nadir,

﴿so We sent upon them a wind﴾ i.e., the east wind (al-Saba). The Prophet ﷺ said, "I was aided by the saba, and 'Ad were destroyed by the dabur,"

﴿and soldiers you did not see﴾, and they were the angels, and they were a thousand. Allah sent upon them a cold east wind on a wintry night, and it besieged them, and it cast dust into their faces, and Allah commanded the angels, so they uprooted the tent pegs, cut the ropes, extinguished the fires, overturned the cooking pots, the horses collided with one another, terror was cast into their hearts, and the angels shouted takbir around the sides of their army, so they fled without fighting. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard of their advance, he dug the trench around Madinah, upon the suggestion of Salman, then he went out with three thousand Muslims, and pitched his camp with the trench between him and the people, and he commanded that the children and the women be lifted up into the fortresses (al-atam), and fear intensified. Quraysh had come with ten thousand, along with (p-20) the Ahabish, Banu Kinanah, and the people of Tihamah, and their commander was Abu Sufyan. Ghatafan went out with a thousand, and those who followed them from the people of Najd, and their commander was Uyaynah ibn Hisn, and Amir ibn al-Tufayl among Hawazin. The Jews of Qurayzah and al-Nadir joined them. About a month passed over the two groups with no fighting between them except the exchange of arrows and stones, until Allah sent down victory.

﴿And Allah is ever Seeing of what you do﴾ i.e., of your deeds, O believers, from fortifying yourselves with the trench and steadfastness in supporting the Prophet ﷺ,

﴿Seeing﴾, and with the letter ya (yabsiru) Abu 'Amr read it, i.e., of what the disbelievers do, of transgression and striving to extinguish the light of Allah.

There is a tension in the request: I'm asked to translate a classical tafsir passage, and the text itself is ordinary exegesis of the verse. The instructions require keeping Qur'anic quotations in ﴿ ﴾ with plain translation of the meaning, and transliterating technical terms. Here the only technical item is none beyond the verse text; no term needs a gloss.

Translation:

﴿There, the believers were tried﴾: they were tested through patience upon faith,

﴿and they were shaken with a mighty shaking﴾: and they were moved by fear with an intense agitation.

**﴿And when the hypocrites say﴾** is coordinated (*'atf*) with the preceding clause.

**﴿And those in whose hearts is a disease﴾**: it is said that this is a description of the hypocrites, with the conjunction *wa* (and) used for description, as in the verse of the poet:

*To the noble king, the son of the resolute one, and the lion of the battalion in the thick of the press.*

It is also said that they are a people who lack insight (*basira*) into the religion. The hypocrites would win them over by planting doubts in their minds.

**﴿What Allah and His Messenger promised us was nothing but delusion﴾**: it is narrated that Mu'attib ibn Qushayr, when he saw the confederates (*al-Ahzab*), said: "Muhammad promises us the conquest of Persia and Byzantium, while none of us can even go out to relieve himself for fear. This is nothing but a promise of delusion."

﴿And when a group of them said﴾, from among the hypocrites, namely ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy and his companions,

﴿O people of Yathrib﴾, they are the people of Madinah,

﴿There is no place to stay for you﴾, and with a ḍamma on the mīm [reading] of Ḥafs (a transmitter of the Qur'anic recitation), meaning: there is no settled place for you here, nor a place where you may stand or remain,

﴿so return﴾, from faith to disbelief, or from the army of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to Madinah,

﴿And a party of them seeks permission from the Prophet﴾ (ﷺ), meaning: the Banu Ḥāritha (p-22),

﴿saying, "Indeed our houses are ʿawrah"﴾, meaning: having a ʿawrah (a vulnerable gap),

﴿But they are not ʿawrah. They only intend to flee﴾. The word ﺍﻟْﻌَﻮْﺭَﺓُ (al-ʿawrah, ʿawra) means a flaw or gap, while ﺍﻟْﻌَﻮِﺭَﺓُ (al-ʿawira, ʿawira) means that which has a gap, and this is the reading of Ibn ʿAbbās. It is said ﻋَﻮِﺭَ ﺍﻟْﻤَﻜَﺎﻥُ ﻋَﻮَﺭًﺍ (ʿawira al-makān ʿawaran, "the place became exposed"), when a flaw appears in it from which the enemy or the thief is feared. It is also permissible that ﻋَﻮْﺭَﺓٌ (ʿawrah) is a lightened form of ﻋَﻮِﺭَﺓٌ (ʿawiratun). They offered the excuse that their houses were exposed to the enemy and the thief because they were not fortified, so they asked him for permission to fortify them and then return to him. Allah refuted them by stating that they did not fear this, and that they only wanted to flee from fighting.

**﴿And if it had been entered upon them﴾** — i.e., the city, or their homes — from the phrase "I entered upon so-and-so, his house" (*dakhaltu ʿalā fulānin dārahu*).

**﴿from its surrounding areas﴾** — from its sides (*jawānibihā*). That is: if these confederate armies, from whom they flee in fear, had entered their city or their homes from all of its directions, and had poured in upon their families and children, plundering and taking captives,

**﴿then they had been asked﴾** — at that moment of terror,

**﴿the fitnah﴾** — i.e., apostasy and returning to disbelief, and fighting the Muslims,

**﴿they would have given it﴾** — they would have granted it. Read as **"la-ātawhā"** without the long vowel (*madd*), according to the Ḥijāzī reading — meaning they would have come to it and done it.

**﴿And they would not have delayed in it﴾** — in answering it,

**﴿except briefly﴾** — just as long as it takes for the question and the answer, without hesitation. Or (the reading is): "They would not have remained in Medina after their apostasy except briefly, then God would destroy them." The meaning is that they make excuses, claiming their houses are exposed, so that they may flee from supporting the Messenger of God ﷺ and the believers, and from confronting the confederates, who have filled them with terror and dread. These confederates are as they are; if they had overrun their land and dwellings, and disbelief had been presented to them, and they had been told, "Stand with the Muslims," they would have hastened to it and made no excuse at all. That is only because of their hatred of Islam and their love of disbelief.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verse 15:

﴿And indeed they had already made a covenant with Allah before, that they would not turn their backs (in flight)﴾. That is: the Banu Haritha, before the (Battle of the) Trench (al-Khandaq), or before their seeing the confederates (al-Ahzab).

﴿They would not turn their backs﴾, i.e., routed (muntahimin).

﴿And the covenant of Allah will be questioned﴾, i.e., demanded (matluban), required (muqtada) until it is fulfilled through it.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verse 16:

(p-٢٣)﴿Say, "Flight will not benefit you if you flee from death or killing; and then you will not be given enjoyment except for a little."﴾ That is: if your appointed term has arrived, flight will not benefit you; and if it has not arrived and you flee, you will not be given enjoyment in this world except for a little, which is the duration of your lives, and that is little. It is related from one of the Marwanids that he passed by a leaning wall and hurried on, so this verse was recited to him, and he said, "It is that little that we seek."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verse 17:

﴿Say, "Who is it that can protect you from Allah?"﴾ That is: from what Allah intends to bring down upon you,

﴿if He intends for you harm﴾, in your persons, by killing or otherwise,

﴿or intends for you mercy﴾, that is: prolonging of life in well-being and safety. That is, who can prevent Allah from showing you mercy if He intends mercy for you? For 'ismah (protection) carries the meaning of prevention,

﴿and they will not find for themselves, besides Allah, any protector (waliyy) or any helper (nasir)﴾, a helper.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verse 18:

﴿Indeed, Allah knows those among you who hinder (others)﴾, that is, those who hinder (people) from supporting the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). "Yu'awwiq" means "yamna'" (prevents). They are the hypocrites (al-munafiqun),

﴿and those who say to their brothers﴾, (who are) outwardly among the Muslims,

﴿"Come here to us"﴾, that is: bring yourselves close to us, and leave Muhammad (ﷺ). This is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz (Hijazi dialect), for they use "halumma" in the same way for the singular and the plural. As for the Tamim, they say: "Halumma, O man" and "Halummu, O men." It is an interjection (sawt) that has been named as a transitive verb, like "ihdar" (be present) and "qarrib" (bring close).

﴿And they do not come to the fight﴾, that is, to the battle,

﴿except a little﴾, meaning, except a little coming: they attend for a moment, out of showing off (riya'), they stand briefly, just enough for their presence to be seen, and then they depart.

﴿أشِحَّةً﴾, the plural of *shaḥīḥ*, meaning *bakhīl* (stingy). It is in the accusative as a *ḥāl* (circumstantial accusative, describing the state of the subject at the time of the action), referring back to the *ḍamīr* (pronoun) in "يَأْتُونَ" (*yaʼtūna*, "they come"). The meaning is: they come to the battle stingy, [grudging] ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ﴾, [towards you], with regard to victory and booty,

﴿فَإذا جاءَ الخَوْفُ﴾, [So when fear comes], from the direction of the enemy, or from him, peace and blessings be upon him, ﴿رَأيْتَهم يَنْظُرُونَ إلَيْكَ﴾, [you see them looking at you], in that state,

﴿تَدُورُ أعْيُنُهُمْ﴾, [their eyes rolling], to the right and to the left,

﴿كالَّذِي يُغْشى عَلَيْهِ مِنَ المَوْتِ﴾, [like one over whom death has come down], as the one who has fainted looks while struggling with the agonies of death, out of fear, cowardice, and clinging to you,

﴿فَإذا ذَهَبَ الخَوْفُ﴾, [But when fear departs], that fear has passed, they feel secure, and the spoils have been collected,

﴿سَلَقُوكم بِألْسِنَةٍ حِدادٍ﴾, [they lash you with sharp tongues], (p-٢٤) they address you with severe speech and harm you with words. "خَطِيبٌ مِسْلَقٌ" (*khaṭībun mislaqun*, "an eloquent orator") means fluent, and "رَجُلٌ مِسْلاقٌ" (*rajulun mislāqun*, "a man of mislāq") means one who is excessive in speech. That is, they say: "Give us our share, for we have witnessed you, fought alongside you, and by our presence you defeated your enemy,"

﴿أشِحَّةً عَلى الخَيْرِ﴾, [stingy towards good], meaning: they address you while being stingy regarding wealth and booty. "أشِحَّةً" is a *ḥāl* from the doer (*fāʻil*, the grammatical subject) of "سَلَقُوكُمْ" (*salaqūkum*, "they lashed you"),

﴿أُولَئِكَ لَمْ يُؤْمِنُوا﴾, [those have not believed], in reality, but only with their tongues,

﴿فَأحْبَطَ اللهُ أعْمالَهُمْ﴾, [so Allah has made their deeds fruitless], He nullified the deeds they displayed, because they concealed disbelief,

﴿وَكانَ ذَلِكَ﴾, [and that was], the nullifying of their deeds,

﴿عَلى اللهِ يَسِيرًا﴾, [easy for Allah], light, effortless.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verse 20:

﴿They think the confederates have not withdrawn﴾, i.e., out of their cowardice they suppose that the confederates have not been routed and have not departed, although in fact they have departed.

﴿And if the confederates should come﴾, a second time,

﴿they would wish that they were in the desert among the Bedouins﴾. "Al-badun" is the plural of "al-badi" (the one dwelling in the desert). That is: the hypocrites, out of their cowardice, wish that they were outside Medina, in the desert, among the Bedouin, so that they would be safe for themselves and would keep away from the fighting in which the believers are engaged.

﴿They ask﴾ every arrival from them, from the direction of Medina,

﴿about your news﴾, i.e., about your reports and what has befallen you.

﴿And if they were among you﴾, and had not returned to Medina, and there were fighting,

﴿they would not fight except a little﴾, for show and for reputation.

﴿Indeed, in the Messenger of God you have an excellent example﴾, read with a damma (ʾuswah) wherever it occurs, by ʿĀṣim, i.e., a model (qudwah), and it is the one who is taken as an example (al-muʾtasā bihi), i.e., the one who is followed (al-muqtadā bihi). This is like when you say: "fī al-bayḍah ʿishrūna mannan ḥadīdan" (in the egg are twenty manns of iron), i.e., the egg itself is this amount of iron; or there is in it a quality which deserves to be emulated, namely that he fought with his own person.

﴿for whoever hopes for God and the Last Day﴾, i.e., fears God and fears the Last Day, or hopes for God's reward and the bliss of the Last Day. They said: "li-man" is a substitute (badal) for "lakum," and this is weak, because substitution from a second-person pronoun (ḍamīr al-mukhāṭab) is not permitted. It was also said that "li-man" is connected to ḥasanah, i.e., an excellent example (ḥasanah) existing for "li-man kāna…" (for whoever was…).

﴿and remembers God much﴾, i.e., in fear, in hope, in hardship and in ease.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verse 22:

﴿When the believers saw the confederates﴾, Allah had promised them that they would be shaken until they called upon Him for help and sought His victory, by His saying: ﴿Do you think that you will enter Paradise while there has not yet come to you the example of those who passed away before you?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 214], up to His saying: ﴿Near﴾ [al-Baqarah: 214]. So when the confederates came, they were agitated and struck with severe terror,

﴿they said: "This is what Allah and His Messenger promised us, and Allah and His Messenger have spoken truly."﴾ They knew that victory and triumph were now assured for them. «It is related from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to his Companions: "The confederates are marching toward you at the end of nine or ten nights." When they saw them approaching at the appointed time, they said that.» And "this" refers to the calamity or the trial.

﴿And it only increased them﴾: what they saw of the gathering of the confederates against them, and their coming,

﴿in faith﴾: in Allah and His promises,

﴿and submission﴾: to His decree and His destiny.

Al-Nasafi, *Madarik al-Tanzil* (commentary on Surah al-Ahzab, 33:23)

﴿Among the believers are men who have been true to what they covenanted with God.﴾ That is, in what they covenanted with Him about. The preposition is omitted, as in the proverb "صَدَقَنِي سِنَّ بَكْرِهِ" (ṣadaqanī sinna bakrihi), meaning "he told me the truth about the age of his young camel." The preposition is dropped and the verb is made to govern its object directly. Some of the Companions (al-Ṣaḥābah) vowed that if they met the enemy in battle alongside the Messenger of God (ﷺ), they would stand firm and fight until they were martyred. They were Uthman ibn Affan, Talhah, Sa'd ibn Zayd, Hamzah, Mus'ab, and others.

﴿Then of them is he who has fulfilled his vow.﴾ That is, he died as a martyr, like Hamzah and Mus'ab. The phrase qaḍāʾ al-naḥb (fulfilling one's vow) came to be an expression for death, because every created living being must die. It is as if death were a binding vow upon one's neck, so when a person dies, he has fulfilled his naḥb, that is, his vow.

﴿And of them is he who waits﴾ for death, (p-26) like Uthman and Talhah.

﴿And they did not change﴾ the covenant

﴿in the least.﴾ Neither the one who was martyred nor the one who waits for martyrdom changed it. This also contains an implicit reproach to those among the hypocrites and the sick of heart who did change, as mentioned in His (exalted) saying: ﴿They had indeed covenanted with God before, that they would not turn their backs.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 15]

لِيَجْزِيَ اللهُ الصادِقِينَ بِصِدْقِهِمْ ("So that Allah may reward the truthful for their truthfulness"), بِوَفائِهِمْ بِالعَهْدِ ("by their fulfilling of the covenant"),

وَيُعَذِّبَ المُنافِقِينَ إنْ شاءَ ("and punish the hypocrites if He wills"), إذا لَمْ يَتُوبُوا ("if they do not repent"),

أوْ يَتُوبَ عَلَيْهِمْ ("or turn to them in forgiveness"), إنْ تابُوا ("if they repent"),

إنَّ اللهَ كانَ غَفُورًا ("Indeed Allah is ever Oft-Forgiving"), بِقَبُولِ التَوْبَةِ ("by accepting repentance"),

رَحِيمًا ("Most Merciful"), بِعَفْوِ الحَوْبَةِ ("by pardoning the sin"). جَعَلَ المُنافِقِينَ كَأنَّهم قَصَدُوا عاقِبَةَ السُوءِ، وأرادُوها بِتَبْدِيلِهِمْ، كَما قَصَدَ الصادِقُونَ عاقِبَةَ الصِدْقِ بِوَفائِهِمْ، لِأنَّ كِلا الفَرِيقَيْنِ مَسُوقٌ إلى عاقِبَتِهِ مِنَ الثَوابِ، والعِقابِ، فَكَأنَّهُما اسْتَوَيا في طَلَبِها، والسَعْيِ في تَحْصِيلِها.

*(He made the hypocrites as though they had intended the consequence of evil and desired it through their changing, just as the truthful intended the consequence of truthfulness through their fulfilling; for both groups are driven toward their consequence of reward and punishment. So it is as if the two were equal in seeking it and striving to attain it.)*

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verse 25:

﴿And Allah turned back those who disbelieved﴾, the confederates (al-Ahzab),

﴿in their rage﴾, a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), meaning: enraged (maghīẓīn), like His saying: ﴿grows with the oil﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 20]. ﴿They did not obtain any good﴾, i.e., victory, meaning: they did not gain victory over the Muslims. He called it "good" according to their own presumption. And it is a circumstantial clause, meaning: not achieving victory (ghayra ẓāfirīn),

﴿And Allah sufficed the believers in fighting﴾, by means of the wind and the angels,

﴿And Allah is ever Strong, Mighty﴾, capable, dominant.

And He brought down those who backed them (﴿وَأنْـزَلَ الَّذِينَ ظاهَرُوهُمْ﴾), that is, those who aided the confederates (عاوَنُوا الأحْزابَ),

from among the People of the Book (﴿مِن أهْلِ الكِتابِ﴾), namely the Banu Qurayza,

from their fortresses (﴿مِن صَياصِيهِمْ﴾), that is, from their strongholds. And "al-ṣayāṣiya" (الصِّيصِيَةُ) is that by which one fortifies oneself. It is narrated that "Jibril (peace be upon him) came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) on the morning of the night in which the confederates were routed and the Muslims had returned to Medina and laid down their weapons, while he was on his horse al-Ḥayzūm, with dust on the horse's face and on the saddle. He said: 'What is this, O Jibril?' He said: 'From pursuing the Quraysh.' So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) began wiping the dust from the horse's face and from its saddle. He (Jibril) said: 'O Messenger of God, the angels have not put down their weapons. God commands you to march against the Banu Qurayza, and I am heading toward them, for God will crush them like eggs crushed upon the rock (al-ṣafā), and they will be prey for you.' So he proclaimed among the people that whoever was listening and obedient should not pray the ʿAṣr prayer except in the land of the Banu Qurayza. They besieged them for twenty-five nights. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'Come down under my judgment.' They refused, so he said: 'Then under the judgment of Saʿd ibn Muʿādh.' They agreed to that. Saʿd said: 'I judge concerning them that their fighting men be killed, and their children and women be taken captive.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said Allahu Akbar and said: 'You have judged by the judgment of God from above the seven heavens.' Then he brought them down, dug a trench in the market of Medina, brought them forward and struck off their necks." They numbered between eight hundred and nine hundred. It was also said that they were six hundred fighting men and seven hundred captives.

﴿وَقَذَفَ في قُلُوبِهِمُ الرُعْبَ﴾, that is, "and He cast terror into their hearts" (al-ruʿb, الْخَوْفَ, meaning fear). The reading with a dammah on the ʿayn (وبِضَمِّ العَيْنِ) is that of Shāmī and ʿAlī (the readers).

﴿فَرِيقًا﴾ is in the accusative by its governing verb ﴿تَقْتُلُونَ﴾, "you kill," and they are the men.

﴿وَتَأْسِرُونَ فَرِيقًا﴾, "and you take captive a group," and they are the women and the children.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verse 27:

﴿And He caused you to inherit their land, their homes and their wealth﴾, i.e., the livestock, the cash, and the goods. It is narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) assigned their real estate to the Muhajirun (emigrants), to the exclusion of the Ansar (helpers), and said to them: "You are in your dwellings,"

﴿and a land you had not trodden﴾, with the intention of fighting. It is Makkah, or Persia and Rome, or Khaybar, and every land until the Day of Resurrection.

﴿And Allah is over all things competent﴾, capable.

O Prophet, say to your wives: "If you desire the life of this world and its adornment," *(i.e., happiness in this world and abundance of wealth)*,

﴿So come, [and] I will provide for you and release you in a fair release.﴾

*Fa-ta'alayna* (﴿so come﴾): the original meaning of *ta'ala* (تَعالَ) is what a person standing in a high place says to someone standing on level ground. It then became common, until places were treated alike in its usage. The meaning of *ta'alayna* (تَعالَيْنَ) is: come by your own will and choice, to one of the two matters. It does not mean that they should rise up towards him by themselves, as in the example *qama yuhaddiduni* (قامَ يُهَدِّدُنِي), "he stood up, threatening me."

﴿Umatti'kunna﴾: I will give you the provision (*mut'at*, مُتْعَةَ) of divorce. Providing *mut'ah* is recommended for every divorced woman, except a *mufawwada* (المُفَوَّضَة, a woman whose dower was left unspecified in the marriage contract) before consummation (*wat'* الوَطْء, marital intercourse).

﴿Wa-usarrihkunna﴾: and I will divorce you,

﴿in a fair release﴾: without harm in it.

They desired something of the world, such as clothing and an increase in maintenance, and they became jealous (of one another), which grieved the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. So this verse was revealed, and he began with ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, who was the dearest of them to him. He offered her the choice and recited the Qur'an to her, and she chose Allah, His Messenger, and the Last Abode. The joy was seen on the face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then all of them chose as she had chosen.

It is also reported that he said to ʿĀʾisha: "I am going to mention a matter to you, and there is no harm if you do not hasten in it until you consult your two parents," then he recited the Qur'an to her. She said: "Regarding this should I consult my parents?! Indeed, I desire Allah, His Messenger, and the Last Abode."

The ruling on giving choice in divorce is that if he says to her, "Choose," and she says, "I have chosen myself," then one irrevocable divorce (*taṭlīqa bā'ina*, تَطْلِيقَةٌ بائِنَةٌ) takes effect. If she chooses her husband, nothing takes effect. It is reported from ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him: "If she chooses her husband, it is one revocable divorce (*raj'iyya*, رَجْعِيَّةٌ); and if she chooses herself, it is one irrevocable divorce."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verse 29:

﴿And if you desire Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode, then indeed Allah has prepared for the good-doers among you [مِنكُنَّ]﴾, "مِن" (min) is for explanation (lil-bayan), not for partition (lil-tab'id),

﴿a great reward﴾

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verse 30:

﴿O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits a clear indecency﴾, an evil act extremely ugly in its ugliness,

﴿manifest﴾, whose indecency is evident, from "bayyana" (to make clear), meaning "tabayyana" (to become clear), and with the letter ya' pronounced with a fatha, which is the reading of Makki and Abu Bakr. It has been said: it is their disobedience to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and their rebelliousness (nushuz). It has also been said: it is fornication (zina), but Allah protects His Messenger from that.

﴿the punishment will be doubled for her﴾, "yudha''if la-ha al-'adhab" (the punishment will be multiplied for her), is read by Makki and Syrian readers as "yudha''af" (with the ya' pointed and the 'ayn doubled), and by Abu 'Amr, Yazid and Ya'qub as "yudha''af" (passive form with the 'ayn doubled).

﴿double﴾, twice the punishment of other women, because what is ugly from other women is uglier when committed by them. The ugliness of disobedience increases in proportion to the increase in excellence, and none of the women has a status like the status of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ. For this reason the blame for a knowing disobedient is more severe than for an ignorant disobedient, since disobedience from one who knows is uglier. For this reason the prescribed punishment (hadd) for free persons exceeds that for slaves, and a disbeliever is not stoned.

﴿And that was﴾, i.e., the doubling of the punishment for them,

﴿with Allah easy﴾, light (hayyin).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verse 31:

﴿Whoever among you (wives of the Prophet) devotes herself (yaqnut) to Allah and His Messenger﴾. "Al-qunut" means obedience (al-ta'ah),

﴿and does righteousness, We will give her reward twice﴾. With the ya' (yu'tiha, yaʾti-style third-person form) in both places: Hamzah and ʿAli (read it this way),

﴿her reward twice﴾, double the reward of others,

﴿and We have prepared for her a generous provision﴾, of noble standing, and it is Paradise.

"O wives of the Prophet, you are not like any one of [other] women."
Meaning: you are not like a single group among the groups of women. When the community of women is examined group by group, there is no single group among them that equals you in merit. And "aḥad" (anyone), originally "waḥad" (one), means the one; then it was placed in general negation, with masculine, feminine, singular and what follows it being equal in it.

﴿If you fear Allah﴾: if you intend taqwa (God-consciousness), or if you are [already] people of taqwa.

﴿So do not be soft in speech﴾: that is, when you speak to men from behind the screen, do not let your speech be yielding (khāḍi'an), i.e., soft and enticing (khanith), like the speech of those who arouse suspicion.

﴿lest one in whose heart is a disease should covet﴾: the verb "fa-yaṭma'a" is in the accusative (naṣb) as an answer to the prohibition (jawāb al-nahy). "Disease" (maraḍ) means doubt (rība) and immorality (fujūr).

﴿but speak in an honorable manner﴾: good speech, while being firm (khashin).

﴿وَقَرْنَ﴾ ("and stay"). Medina and ʿĀṣim (readers), except Hubayra, read it as ﴿وَقَرْنَ﴾. Its original form is "اِقْرَرْنَ" (iqrarna). The first "را" was elided for lightness, and its vowel (fatḥa) was transferred to the letter before it. Alternatively, it derives from "قارَّ، يَقارُّ" (qārra, yaqārru), meaning "to gather." The rest of the readers read "قِرْنَ" (qirna), from "وَقَرَ، وقارًا" (waqara, waqāran, "to be dignified and settled") or from "قَرَّ، يَقَرُّ" (qarra, yaqarru, "to settle"). In that case the first of the two identical letters ("ر") was elided, meaning "اِقْرَرْنَ، قَرارًا" (iqrarna, qarāran), from "التَكْرارِ" (repetition). The kasra of its vowel was moved to the "ق" (qāf).

﴿فِي بُيُوتِكُنَّ﴾ ("in your houses"), with the "ب" (bāʾ) pronounced with a ḍamma, read by Baṣrī, Madanī and Ḥafṣ.

﴿وَلا تَبَرَّجْنَ تَبَرُّجَ الجاهِلِيَّةِ الأُولى﴾ ("and do not display yourselves as in the former times of ignorance"). That is, "اَلْقَدِيمَةِ" (the ancient). (p-30) "Tabarruj" means walking coquettishly, or displaying adornment. The implied sense is: "وَلا تَبَرَّجْنَ تَبَرُّجًا مِثْلَ تَبَرُّجِ النِساءِ في الجاهِلِيَّةِ الأُولى" ("do not display yourselves in a manner like the display of women in the former times of ignorance"). The "former ignorance" is the period in which Ibrahim was born, or the period between Adam and Nuh (peace be upon them both), or between Dawud and Sulayman. The "later ignorance" is the period between ʿĪsā and Muḥammad (peace be upon them both). Alternatively, the "former ignorance" is the ignorance of disbelief before Islam, and the "later ignorance" is the ignorance of wickedness and immorality within Islam.

﴿وَأقِمْنَ الصَلاةَ وآتِينَ الزَكاةَ وأطِعْنَ اللهَ ورَسُولَهُ﴾ ("and establish the prayer, give the zakat, and obey Allah and His Messenger"). He singled out the prayer and zakat for the command, then generalized to all acts of obedience, to honour them, because whoever is constant in them is led by them to what lies beyond them.

﴿إنَّما يُرِيدُ اللهُ لِيُذْهِبَ عَنْكُمُ الرِجْسَ أهْلَ البَيْتِ﴾ ("Allah only wants to remove uncleanness from you, O People of the House"). "Ahl al-Bayt" is in the accusative, either as a vocative (in address) or as a laudatory appositive (in praise). It indicates that his wives are among the People of the House. He said "عَنْكُمْ" ("from you," masculine plural), because men and women of his family are both intended, as shown by ﴿وَيُطَهِّرَكم تَطْهِيرًا﴾ ("and purify you with a thorough purification"), that is, from the filth of sins. Then he explained that he forbade them, commanded them and admonished them only so that the People of the House of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would not commit sins, and would guard themselves against them through piety. He used "الرِجْسَ" (uncleanness) as a metaphor for sins, and "الطُهْرَ" (purity) for piety, because the honour of one who commits abominable acts becomes stained by them, just as his body becomes stained by filth. As for those who act virtuously, their honour is pure, like a clean garment. In this there is a warning to people of understanding against what is forbidden, and an encouragement for them toward what is commanded.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verse 34:

﴿And remember what is recited in your houses of the signs of Allah﴾, namely the Qur'an,

﴿and the wisdom﴾, i.e., the Sunnah (the Prophetic practice and teachings), or the explanation of the meanings of the Qur'an,

﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Subtle﴾, knowing the hidden subtleties of things,

﴿Aware﴾, knowing their realities. That is, He knows your deeds and your words. So beware of opposing His command and His prohibition, and of disobeying His Messenger.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verse 35:

When there was revealed concerning the wives of the Prophet ﷺ what was revealed, the women of the believers said: "Nothing has been revealed concerning us." So there was revealed: ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and the Muslim women﴾. "Al-muslim" (the one who submits): one who enters into peace (silm) after war, the compliant one who does not obstinately oppose, or one who entrusts his affair to Allah and relies upon Him, "one who has submitted his face (aslama wajhahu) to Allah,"

﴿and the believing men﴾, those who affirm (musaddiqin) Allah and His Messenger, and what must be affirmed,

﴿and the believing women, and the devout men﴾, those who stand in obedience (al-qa'imin bil-ta'ah),

﴿and the devout women, and the truthful men﴾, in intentions, statements, and deeds,

﴿and the truthful women, and the patient men and the patient women﴾, in acts of obedience and in refraining from sins,

﴿and the humble men﴾, those who are humbly submissive to Allah with their hearts and limbs, or those who fear (Him),

﴿and the humble women, and the almsgiving men and the almsgiving women﴾, in obligatory and voluntary charity,

﴿and the fasting men and the fasting women﴾, in obligatory and voluntary fasting. It is said: whoever gives charity of one dirham each week is among the almsgivers, and whoever fasts the white days (al-bid) of each month is among the fasting.

﴿and the men who guard their private parts, and the women who guard﴾, from what is not lawful,

﴿and the men and women who remember Allah often﴾, through glorification (tasbih), praise (tahmid), declaration of His oneness (tahlil), magnification (takbir), recitation of the Qur'an, and occupation with knowledge, which is a form of remembrance. The meaning is: "and the women who guard their private parts, and the women who remember Allah," and the second element has been omitted because of what preceded it. The difference between coordinating females with males and coordinating the two spouses with each other is that the former is like His saying: ﴿previously married and virgins﴾ [al-Tahrim: 5], in that they are two different categories that share a single ruling, so there was no alternative to placing the conjunction between them; whereas the latter is the coordination of an attribute with an attribute by means of the conjunction of plurality, and its meaning is that those who combine these acts of obedience, both men and women,

﴿Allah has prepared for them forgiveness and a great reward﴾, in return for their obedience.

Al-Nasafi, Madarik al-Tanzil (commentary) on Surah al-Ahzab (33), verse 36:

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) proposed marriage to Zaynab bint Jahsh, the daughter of his paternal aunt Umayma, on behalf of his freed slave Zayd ibn Harithah. She refused, and her brother Abdullah refused too. So the verse was revealed: ﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman﴾, meaning: it is not proper for a believing man or a believing woman,

﴿when Allah and His Messenger have decreed a matter﴾, meaning: the Messenger of Allah,

﴿that they should have any choice in their affair﴾, meaning: that they should choose whatever they wish concerning their affair. Rather, it is their right to make their opinion follow his opinion, and their choice follow his choice. So they both said: "We are pleased, O Messenger of Allah." He then married her to him, and gave her dowry on his behalf.

He used the plural pronoun in "lahum" (for them), although it should have been singular, because the two mentioned (the man and the woman) fall under negation, so it covers every believing man and every believing woman. The pronoun therefore refers to the meaning, not to the wording. The reading "yakuna" with the ya (third person) is that of Kufan (the Kufan reciters). "Al-khiyara" means that which is chosen. This indicates that the imperative here implies obligation.

﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly strayed into clear error﴾. If the disobedience is disobedience of rejection and refusal to accept, then it is the error of disbelief (kufr). If it is disobedience in action while accepting the command and believing it obligatory, then it is the error of mistake and grave sin (fisq).

﴿And when you said to the one on whom Allah had bestowed favor﴾ with Islam, which is the greatest of favors,

﴿and you had bestowed favor upon him﴾ with manumission and adoption. So he was living in the favor of Allah and the favor of His Messenger. He was Zayd ibn Harithah.

﴿Keep your wife to yourself﴾, Zaynab bint Jahsh. The reason was that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw her after he had married her to him, and she fell into his heart. He said: "Glory be to Allah, the Turner of hearts." The reason was that his own self had previously been averse to her and did not desire her. Zaynab heard the glorification (tasbihah) and mentioned it to Zayd, and he understood. Allah placed in his heart the aversion to her company and the desire to be free of her for the sake of the Messenger of Allah. "So he said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: 'I want to separate from my companion.' He said: 'What is the matter with you? Has something about her made you doubt?' He said: 'No, by Allah, I have seen nothing from her but good, but she exalts herself over me because of her nobility, and she hurts me.' So he said to him: ﴿Keep your wife to yourself and fear Allah﴾, so do not divorce her." This is a prohibition of discouragement (nahy tanzih, a prohibition indicating what is better to avoid), since the better course is not to divorce, or "and fear Allah," so do not blame her in respect of pride and harm to the husband.

﴿And you concealed within yourself that which Allah was to disclose﴾, meaning: you concealed within yourself the marriage to her if Zayd divorced her, and this is what Allah disclosed. It was said: what he concealed within himself was the attachment of his heart to her and his love for Zayd's separation from her. The waw in "and you concealed within yourself" is ...

﴿and you feared the people﴾, meaning: the people's saying, "He married his son's wife."

﴿And Allah has more right that you fear Him﴾. The waw is the waw of circumstance (waw al-hal). Meaning: you say to Zayd, "Keep your wife to yourself," while concealing within yourself the desire that he not keep her. And you conceal, fearing the people's talk, and you fear the people in truth in that matter, by fearing Allah. "On the authority of Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her: 'If the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had concealed anything of what was revealed to him, he would have concealed this verse.'"

﴿So when Zayd had no longer any need of her﴾. "Al-wataṭ" (need, requirement) means need. When a person reaches his need in something in which he has an aspiration, it is said: "He fulfilled his wataṭ from it." The meaning: when Zayd no longer had any need for her, and his aspiration fell short of her, and he divorced her, and her waiting period ended,

﴿We married her to you﴾. It is narrated that when she had completed her waiting period, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Zayd: "I find no one more trustworthy in my soul than you. Propose on my behalf to Zaynab." Zayd said: "So I went and said: 'O Zaynab, rejoice, for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is proposing to you.' She rejoiced, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married her, and consummated the marriage with her. He did not hold a wedding feast for any of his wives as he held for her. He slaughtered a sheep and fed the people bread and meat until the day was prolonged."

﴿So that there will be no discomfort for the believers concerning the wives of their adopted sons when they have no longer any need of them﴾. It was said: the fulfillment of the wataṭ is attaining the need and reaching the desired aim from it.

﴿And the command of Allah is ever accomplished﴾, that which He wills to be,

﴿an accomplished matter﴾, a certainty that will certainly occur. This is an example of what He willed to come to be, namely the marriage of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to Zaynab.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verse 38:

﴿There is no restriction upon the Prophet in what Allah has ordained for him﴾. It was made lawful for him and he was commanded to do it, namely the marriage to Zaynab, the wife of Zayd; or it was decreed for him concerning the number of wives.

﴿The way of Allah﴾: "sunnata" (way, practice) is a noun placed in the position of the verbal noun (masdar), like their saying "turaban" (dust) and "jandalan" (rock). It emphasizes His saying: ﴿There is no restriction upon the Prophet﴾, as if it was said: "Allah established that as a way (sunnah) among the earlier Prophets, which is that He would not impose hardship upon them in proceeding with what He permitted for them, and He widened for them in the matter of marriage and other things." Indeed, they had concubines and slave-girls under them. David had one hundred wives and three hundred concubines, and Solomon had three hundred free wives and seven hundred concubines.

﴿Among those who passed away before﴾: among the Prophets who passed away before.

﴿And the command of Allah is a decree determined﴾: a decree decided, and a judgment absolutely fixed. There is no pause at it if you make it so.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verse 39:

﴿Those who convey the messages of Allah﴾, in apposition (badal) to the first "alladhina" (those). Pause (waqf) here if you take it to be in the nominative or accusative position, by way of praise (al-madh), meaning: "They are the ones who convey," or: "I mean those who convey."

﴿And they fear Him and fear no one except Allah﴾. The description of the prophets as fearing none but Allah is an indirect allusion (ta'rid) following the explicit statement in His words: "And you feared the people, while Allah has more right that you should fear Him."

﴿And Allah suffices as a Reckoner﴾: sufficient for all fears, and one who takes account of the small and the great, so He is worthy that you should fear Him.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verse 40:

﴿Muhammad is not the father of any one of your men﴾. That is: he was not truly the father of any man among you, such that there would hold between him and them what holds between a father and his son, of the prohibition of marriage by affinity (ḥurmat al-ṣihr) and marriage (al-nikāḥ). What is meant by "your men" is those who have reached maturity (al-bāligūn). al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn were not mature at that time, and al-Ṭāhir, al-Ṭayyib, al-Qāsim and Ibrahim died as children.

﴿But﴾ he was,

﴿the Messenger of Allah﴾. Every messenger is a father to his community, in respect of the obligation of honouring and magnifying him on their part, and the obligation of compassion and sincere counsel on his part toward them, in all the rulings that hold between fathers and sons. Zayd is one of your men who is not truly his son, so his ruling is the same as your ruling. Adoption (al-tabanni) is a matter of special closeness and nearness, and nothing more.

﴿And the Seal of the Prophets﴾, with a fatḥa on the tā'. ʿĀṣim read it so, in the sense of "al-ṭābaʿ" (the seal), that is: the last of them. It means that no one will be sent as a prophet after him. ʿĪsā is among those who were prophesied before him, and when he descends, he will descend acting according to the law (sharīʿa) of Muhammad (ﷺ), as if he were one of his community. Others read it with a kasra on the tā', in the sense of "al-ṭābiʿ" (the one who seals), the agent of the sealing. The reading of Ibn Masʿūd strengthens this: "but a Prophet who sealed the Prophets."

﴿And Allah is ever Knowing of all things﴾
O you who have believed, remember Allah with much remembrance (﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اذْكُرُوا اللهَ ذِكْرًا كَثِيرًا﴾). Praise Him with all kinds of praise, and be abundant in that.

﴿And glorify Him at dawn﴾, at the beginning of the day,

﴿and in the evening﴾, at the end of the day. These two were singled out for mention because the angels of the night and the angels of the day gather at them. It is related from Qatadah: "Say: 'Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and there is no god but Allah, and Allah is greatest, and there is no power nor strength except through Allah, the Most High, the Mighty.'" The two verbs, i.e. "remember Allah" and "glorify Him," are directed at the morning and the evening, like your saying: "Fast and pray on Friday." Glorification (al-tasbih) (the act of declaring Allah free of imperfection) is part of remembrance (al-dhikr). It was singled out from among its kinds in the way that Jibril and Mika'il were singled out from among the angels, to demonstrate its excellence over the other forms of remembrance, because its meaning is declaring His essence free of the attributes that are not befitting for Him. It is also permissible that what is meant by remembrance and its frequency is the multiplication of acts of obedience and worship, for these are part of remembrance. Then He singled out from this glorification the time of "bukrah" (dawn), which is the Fajr prayer, and "asil" (evening), which is the Zuhr, 'Asr, Maghrib and 'Isha' prayers, or the Fajr and the two 'Ishas (the 'Isha' and the evening prayer after sunset).

He it is who showers blessings upon you, and His angels (do so as well), ﴿He it is who showers blessings upon you, and His angels (do so as well)﴾. Since it is in the nature of one who prays to bend in his bowing and prostration, the word was borrowed for one who inclines toward another out of tenderness and compassion, like the visitor of the sick in his leaning over him, and the mother in her tenderness toward her child. Then it became common until it was used for mercy and compassion. From this comes their saying, "Allah bless you" (ﷺ-style invocation), meaning: "May He have mercy upon you and show you compassion." The intended meaning of the blessing of the angels is their saying, "O Allah, bless the believers," and they are given this (sense) because they are those whose supplication is answered, as if they were the ones who bring about mercy and tenderness. The meaning is: "He it is who has mercy upon you, and who shows compassion when He calls you to goodness, and commands you to remember Him much and to devote yourselves to prayer and obedience."

﴿That He may bring you out of the darkness into the light﴾, from the darknesses of disobedience to the light of obedience.

﴿And He is ever Merciful to the believers﴾. This is evidence that the meaning of "blessing" here is mercy. It is narrated that when the verse "Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet" (al-Ahzab: 56) was revealed, Abu Bakr said, "O Messenger of Allah, Allah has not singled you out with any honour except that He has made us partners in it." Then the verse was revealed:

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verse 44:

﴿Their greeting﴾ is from the addition of the verbal noun (maṣdar) to its object (mafʿūl), meaning: God's greeting to them,

﴿on the day they meet Him﴾, meaning: they see Him,

﴿will be "Peace"﴾. God, blessed and exalted, says: "Peace be upon you,"

﴿and He has prepared for them a generous reward﴾, meaning: Paradise.

O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness, over whom you were sent to them and over their denial and their affirmation; meaning, your word concerning them and against them being accepted by Allah, just as the word of an upright witness is accepted in judgment. This is a hal muqaddarah (a future or anticipated circumstantial clause), as you say: "I passed by a man with a falcon, hunting with it tomorrow," meaning: one who will be hunting with it tomorrow.

And a bringer of good tidings to the believers of Paradise,

And a warner to the disbelievers of the Fire.

﴿And as one who calls to Allah by His permission﴾, that is, by His command and by His facilitation. All of these (words) are in the accusative as circumstantial clauses (ḥāl).

﴿And as a radiant lamp﴾. Through him Allah dispelled the darknesses of polytheism, and those who had gone astray were guided by him, just as the darkness of the night is dispelled by a bright lamp and one is guided by it. The majority of scholars hold that this refers to the Qur'an, so the implied construction is: "and (as) one possessing a radiant lamp," or: "and reciting a radiant lamp." It is described as radiant (munīr) because some lamps do not give light when their oil (salīṭ) is scanty and their wick (fatīla) is thin. Alternatively, the meaning is: "a witness to Our oneness, a bearer of good news of Our mercy, a warner of Our punishment, one who calls to Our worship, and a lamp and a manifest proof for Our presence."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verse 47:

﴿And give good tidings to the believers that they will have from Allah a great bounty﴾, a great reward.

And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites. What is meant by this is to stir up (the Prophet's resolve), or it means continuing and remaining steadfast in what he was already doing.

﴿And disregard their harm﴾. It has the meaning of causing harm (idha'), so it may be an annexed construction (mudaf) with the agent, meaning: "Make their harm to you a matter of no concern, do not care about them, and do not fear their harm." Or it may be annexed to the object, meaning: "Set aside your harming them in retaliation against them."

﴿And put your trust in Allah﴾, for He is sufficient for you against them.

﴿And Allah is sufficient as a Guardian﴾. Allah is sufficient as one in whom affairs are entrusted. It has been said that Allah (exalted is He) described him with five attributes and matched each of them with a suitable address (p-٣٧). He matched the witness with His words, "and give good news to the believers," because he is a witness over his community, and they are witnesses over the rest of the nations, and this is the great favour. He matched the bearer of good news with turning away from the disbelievers and the hypocrites, because when he turns away from them he directs his full attention to the believers, and this suits the good news. He matched the warner with "and disregard their harm," because when he leaves off harming them in the present (and harm must bring punishment, sooner or later), they are warned of it in the future. He matched the one who calls to Allah with facilitation, through His words, "and put your trust in Allah," for whoever trusts in Allah, every hardship is made easy for him. And He matched the illuminating lamp with being sufficed by Him as a Guardian, for whoever Allah has illuminated with proof over all His creation is worthy of being sufficed by Him over all His creation.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verse 49:

﴿O you who have believed, when you marry believing women⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿ ...﴾ That is: when you wed (tazawwajtum). Nikah (marriage; the word literally denotes sexual intercourse, and its use for the contract is metaphorical) is in origin intercourse, and naming the contract "nikah" is due to its being connected to it, in that it is the means to it, just as wine is called "sin" (ithm) because it is its cause, and as in the verse of the rajaz poet:

"The humps of the camels in its clouds"

He called the water "the humps of the camels," because it is the cause of the camels' fattening and the rising of their humps. The word nikah does not occur in the Book of Allah (exalted is He) except with the meaning of the contract, since it carries the meaning of intercourse as an explicit term. Among the etiquette of the Qur'an is to refer to it by euphemisms such as mulamasah (touching), mumassah (contact), qurban (approaching), taghashshi (covering) and ityan (coming to). In singling out believing women — although the women of the People of the Book share this ruling with them — there is an indication that it is preferable for a believer to marry a believing woman.

﴿Then you divorce them before you have touched them⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿...﴾ And valid seclusion (khalwah sahihah) is equivalent to touching.

﴿...then you have no waiting period for them to count⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿...﴾ In this is evidence that the waiting period (iddah) is owed by women to men. The meaning of "ta'taddunaha" is: you complete its number; it is of the form "ta'tadilun," from "al-add" (counting).

﴿So provide for them⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿...﴾ Provision (mut'ah) is obligatory for the woman whom he divorced before consummation and for whom no dower was specified, and not for others.

﴿And release them with a fair release⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿...﴾ That is: do not keep them by way of harm, and send them out of your homes, since you have no waiting period owed to you over them.

(p-38) ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful for you your wives to whom you have given their ujur (compensation)﴾: meaning their mahr (bridal gift). The mahr is a ajr (compensation) for the bid' (intercourse). For this reason al-Karkhi said: "A nikah (marriage contract) with the wording of ijara (contract of hire) is permissible." We reply: "Permanence (al-ta'bid) is a condition of nikah, while limitation in time (al-ta'qit) is a condition of ijara, and there is a contradiction between them." Ita'uha (giving them) means giving them promptly, or fixing them (as an obligation), or naming them in the contract.

﴿and what your right hand possesses of what Allah has granted you as spoils﴾: these were Safiyya and Juwayriya. He freed them and married them.

﴿and the daughters of your paternal uncles, the daughters of your paternal aunts, the daughters of your maternal uncles, and the daughters of your maternal aunts, who emigrated with you﴾: the word "ma'a" (with) does not indicate simultaneity (al-qiran), but merely existence together, as in His saying: ﴿and I submitted with Solomon﴾ [an-Naml: 44]. And from Umm Hani bint Abi Talib: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) proposed to me, and I excused myself, so he excused me, and Allah revealed this verse. So I was not lawful to him, because I had not emigrated with him."

﴿and a believing woman, if she gives herself to the Prophet﴾: We have made lawful for you what occurs for her, that she gives herself to you and does not seek a mahr, from among the believing women, if that happens. For this reason He made her indefinite (nakkaraha, "a woman" without a specific identity). Ibn 'Abbas said: "This is a statement of a ruling for the future, and none of them had given herself in gift to him at that time." It was said that the woman who gave herself was Maymuna bint al-Harith, or Zaynab bint Khuzayma, or Umm Sharik bint Jabir, or Khawla bint Hakim. Al-Hasan read "an" (that) with a fatha, as a causative (al-ta'lil), with the lam omitted by implication. Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) read it without "in" (if).

﴿if the Prophet desires to take her in marriage﴾: istinkahuha means seeking her marriage and desire for it. It was also said that "nakaha" and "istankaha" have the same meaning. The second condition restricts the first condition. The condition for the permission is her giving herself in gift, and in the gift is the desire of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to take her in marriage. It is as if He said: "We have made her lawful for you if she gives herself to you, while you wish to take her in marriage," because his desire is the acceptance of the gift and what completes it. In this there is evidence for the permissibility of nikah with the wording of hibah (gift), because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his community are equal in the rulings, except in what is specific to him. The evidence is ﴿khalisatan﴾ (exclusively), without a mahr, which is a ḥal (state word) from the pronoun in (p-39) "wahabat" (she gave), or an emphatic infinitive (masdar mu'akkid), meaning: the permission of what We have permitted for you became exclusive for you, in the sense of "khulusan" (exclusivity). The active participle form in the verbal nouns is not "'aziz" (strong), like "al-'afiya" and "al-kadhiba" (the feminine forms used as nouns).

﴿for you alone, apart from the believers﴾: rather, the mahr becomes obligatory for others, even if it was not named or was denied. He shifted from address to third person in His saying "if the Prophet desires," then returned to address, to indicate that the exclusivity is an honour for him because of prophethood. And its repetition, meaning the repetition of "al-Nabiyy" (the Prophet), is an exaltation of him.

﴿We have indeed known what We have imposed upon them concerning their wives﴾: that is, what We have made obligatory of mahrs upon your community concerning their wives, or what We have made obligatory upon them concerning their wives of rights.

﴿and what their right hands possess﴾: by purchase or other modes of ownership. His saying ﴿so that there may be no hardship upon you﴾ means narrowness (ḥaraj), and is connected to "exclusively for you, apart from the believers." His saying "We have indeed known what We have imposed upon them concerning their wives and what their right hands possess" is an interpolated clause (jumla i'tirad iyya).

﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾: by granting ease to His servants.

﴿Turji﴾, without a hamza, is the reading of Madani, Hamzah, Ali, Khalaf and Hafs. The other readers recite it with a hamza, as ﴿tu'akhkhiru﴾ ("you defer").

﴿whom you will among them, and you take to yourself whom you will﴾: "tadummu" (you take in) means: you leave off lying with whomever of them you will, and you lie with whomever you will; or you divorce whomever you will and keep whomever you will; or you do not divide your time equally among whichever of them you wish, and you divide it among whomever you wish; or you leave off marrying whomever you wish from among the women of your community, and you marry whomever you wish. This is a comprehensive division covering the whole matter, because he either divorces or keeps. If he keeps, he lies with her, or he leaves her and divides his time, or he does not divide it. If he divorces and separates from her, then either he leaves the separated wife alone and does not seek her, or he seeks her. It is narrated that he deferred (the turn of) Juwayriyah, Sawdah, Safiyyah, Maymunah and Umm Habibah, and he divided his time among them as he wished, in the manner he wished. Those whom he took to himself were ʿĀʾishah, Ḥafṣah, Umm Salamah and Zaynab. He deferred five and took four to himself. It is also narrated that he (p-40) used to treat them equally, despite the latitude given to him and the choice granted to him in this matter, except Sawdah, for she gave her night to ʿĀʾishah and said: "Do not divorce me, so that I may be raised on the Day of Resurrection in the company of your wives."

﴿And whomever you seek out from among those you have set aside, there is no blame upon you﴾: that is, whomever you invite to your bed and seek companionship with, from among those you have set aside from yourself by deferral, there is no restriction upon you in that. That is, it is not the case that once you have set her aside it is impermissible for you to take her back to yourself. "Man" (whoever) is in the nominative as the subject, and its predicate is "fa-la junaha" (there is no blame).

﴿That﴾: the delegation of the matter to your will.

﴿That is more suitable that their eyes may be comforted, and that they may not grieve, and that they may all be content with what you give them﴾: that is, it is closer to the comfort of their eyes, to lessening their grief, and to all of them being content, because when they know that this delegation comes from God, their souls are set at rest, jealousy departs, contentment is attained, and eyes are comforted. "Kulluhunna" (all of them), in the nominative, is an emphatic reinforcement of the "nun" in "yardayna" (they are content). It is also read: "wa-yardayna kulluhunna bi-ma atayta-hunna" (with the word order altered), and an anomalous reading (shadhdh) has "kullahunna" in the accusative, as an emphasis on the "hunna" in "atayta-hunna".

﴿And God knows what is in your hearts﴾: this contains a warning to whoever among them is not content with what God has ordained in this matter and delegated to the will of His Messenger.

﴿And God is ever Knowing﴾: of what is within the breasts,

﴿Forbearing﴾: He does not hasten to punish, so He is worthy of being feared and guarded against.

﴿Lā yaḥillu laka al-nisā'﴾ ("It is not lawful for you [to take] women"). Abu 'Amr and Ya'qub read it with the feminine ta' (tā'), while the others read it with the masculine (tadhkīr), because the feminine of a plural is not a true feminine (ta'nīth ghayr ḥaqīqī). If it is permitted without a separating element in ﴿Wa qāla niswatun﴾ [Yusuf: 30], then with a separating element it is even more permissible.

﴿Min ba'du﴾ ("after this"): i.e., after the nine, because nine is the quota (niṣāb) of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in wives, just as four is the quota of his community.

﴿Wa lā an tabaddala bihinna min azwāj﴾ ("nor that you should exchange them for other wives"): by divorce. The meaning is: nor that you should substitute for these nine other wives, either all of them or some of them, as an honour to them and a reward for what they chose and were content with. Thus the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was restricted to them, and they are the nine whom he left at his death: ʿĀ'isha, Ḥafṣa, Umm Ḥabība, Sawda, Umm Salama, Ṣafiyya, Maymuna, Zaynab bint Jaḥsh, and Juwayriya. The "min" in "min azwāj" is for emphasis of the negation, and its purpose is to encompass the whole category of wives with the prohibition.

﴿Wa law a'jabaka ḥusnuhunna﴾ ("even if their beauty pleased you"): this is in the position of a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) relating to the agent, which is the pronoun in "tabaddala", meaning "tatabaddala" [i.e., the verb's subject], and not relating to the object which is "min azwāj", because of its extreme indefiniteness (tawaghghul fī al-tankīr). Its implied construction is: "your admiration for them being assumed." It is said that this refers to Asma' bint 'Umays, the wife of Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, since she was among those whose beauty pleased him. It is also reported from 'Ā'isha and Umm Salama: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not die until it was made lawful for him to marry from among women whatever he wished." They mean that the verse was abrogated (nusikhat). Its abrogation was either by the Sunna, or by His saying: ﴿Innā aḥlalnā laka azwājaka﴾ [al-Aḥzab: 50]. The order of revelation is not according to the order of the Mushaf (the codex).

﴿Illā mā malakat yamīnuka﴾ ("except what your right hand possesses"): an exception from those whom he was forbidden to take, namely the female slaves (imā'). The place of "mā" is nominative (raf'), as a substitute (badal) for "al-nisā'".

﴿Wa kāna Allāhu 'alā kulli shay'in raqīban﴾ ("And Allah is ever Watchful over all things"): i.e., Guardian (ḥāfiẓan). This is a warning against transgressing His limits.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (*Madarik al-Tanzil*) on surah 33, verse 53:

﴿O you who believe, do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless permission is given you for a meal, without waiting for its preparation.﴾ "*An yu'dhana lakum*" (that permission be given you) is in the position of a *hal* (circumstantial accusative, describing the state of the subject at the time of the action). The meaning is: do not enter except being permitted. Or it is in the sense of a *zarf* (temporal adverb), its implied meaning being: except at the time when permission is given you. "*Ghayra nazhirin*" (without waiting) is a *hal* of "*la tadkhulu*" (do not enter). The exception applies to both the time and the state together, as if it were said: "Do not enter the houses of the Prophet except at the time of permission, and do not enter them except without waiting." *Nazhirin* means *muntazhirin* (waiting). These were people who would watch for the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ food, enter, and sit waiting for it to be ready. The meaning is: "Do not enter, O you who lie in wait for the food, except when you are given permission to a meal, without waiting for its preparation." "*Inan al-ta'am*" means its ripening (its being cooked). It is said: "*anā al-ta'āmu inan*," like your saying: "*qalāhu, qilan*" (he disliked it, a disliking). It is also said: "*ināhu*" means its time, that is: without waiting for the time of the food and the hour of its eating.

It is narrated that the Prophet ﷺ held a wedding feast for Zaynab with dates, roasted barley flour, and a sheep, and he commanded Anas to invite the people. They came in successive groups: one group would eat and leave, then another group would enter, until Anas said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have invited people until I can find no one left to invite." He said: "Lift up your food." The people dispersed, but three men remained, talking, and they prolonged it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up so that they would leave, and he went around the apartments, greeted the wives, and they prayed for him. He returned, and found the three still sitting and talking. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was extremely shy, so he turned away. When they saw him turning away, they left. Then he returned, and the verse was revealed:

﴿But when you are invited, then enter; and when you have eaten, then disperse﴾, so they dispersed.

﴿Nor lingering for conversation﴾: it is in the genitive case (*majrur*), coordinated with "*nazhirin*," or it is in the accusative case (*mansub*), meaning: "and do not enter it lingering." They were forbidden to prolong sitting, such that some of them would keep one another company for the sake of a talk one of them would relate.

﴿Indeed, that would cause the Prophet inconvenience, and he would be shy of you﴾, [shy] of your leaving.

﴿But Allah is not shy of the truth﴾: meaning that your leaving is the truth, and it is not something one should be shy about. Since shyness is something that prevents the shy person from certain actions, it was said: "He is not shy of the truth," that is: He does not refrain from it, nor does He leave it out out of the shyness that you show. This is a courtesy with which Allah taught the burdensome guests.
