It is narrated from ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her: "It is enough of a judgment against burdensome guests that Allah (exalted is He) did not tolerate them, and said: ﴿But when you have eaten, then disperse﴾ ﴿And when you ask them for something﴾." The pronoun refers to the wives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, since the houses of the Prophet indicate them, because his wives are in them.

﴿Something﴾: a loan, or a need.

﴿Then ask them﴾: for the item.

﴿From behind a screen. That is purer for your hearts and their hearts﴾: from the thoughts of Satan and the onset of temptations. Before the revelation of this verse, women would appear before men. ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, loved to have a screen set up for them and wished that it would be revealed concerning this. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, the pious and the wicked enter upon you. If only you would command the Mothers of the Believers to observe the veil." Then it was revealed. It is mentioned that some of them said: "Are we forbidden to speak with our cousins except from behind a screen? If Muhammad dies, I will marry so-and-so." Then it was revealed: ﴿It is not for you to harm the Messenger of Allah, nor to marry his wives after him, ever﴾, meaning: it is not correct for you to harm the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, nor to marry his wives after his death.

﴿Indeed, that is in the sight of Allah an enormous (sin)﴾, meaning: a great sin.

If you disclose a thing, [whether it is] harming the Prophet ﷺ or [marrying] his wives, or you conceal it within yourselves regarding that, then indeed Allah is ever, of all things, Knowing; so He will punish you for it.

When the verse of hijab was revealed, the fathers, sons, and relatives said, "O Messenger of Allah, are we also to speak to them from behind a veil?" Then it was revealed: ﴿There is no blame upon them concerning their fathers, their sons, their brothers, the sons of their brothers, the sons of their sisters, or their women,﴾ meaning the women of the believers,

﴿nor what their right hands possess.﴾ Meaning, there is no sin upon them in not veiling before these. He did not mention the paternal uncle or the maternal uncle, because they are treated as the two parents, and the paternal uncle has been called "father." Allah the Exalted said: ﴿the God of your fathers, Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac﴾ [al-Baqarah: 133], and Ishmael was the uncle of Jacob.

As for their slaves, according to the majority (al-Jumhur) they are treated as strangers. Then the speech shifted from the third person (al-ghaybah) to the second person (al-khitab). In this shift there is an added emphasis, as if it were said: ﴿and fear Allah﴾ regarding what you have been commanded concerning veiling, and be attentive to the revelation concerning concealment, and be cautious in it.

﴿Indeed, Allah is ever, over all things, Witness,﴾ meaning knowing. Ibn ʿAtaʾ said: "al-Shahid" (the Witness) is the One who knows the passing thoughts of hearts just as He knows the movements of the limbs.

(p-44) ﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who have believed, send blessings upon him and greet him with peace.﴾ That is: say, "O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad," or "May Allah bless Muhammad."

﴿And greet him with abundant peace﴾ That is: say, "O Allah, grant peace upon Muhammad," or submit to his command and judgment with full submission.

He (upon him be blessings and peace) was asked about this verse and said: "Indeed, Allah has appointed two angels for me. No one mentions me in the presence of a Muslim servant who then sends blessings upon me, except that those two angels say: 'May Allah forgive you,' and Allah and His angels respond to those two angels: 'Amin.' And no one mentions me in the presence of a Muslim servant who does not send blessings upon me, except that those two angels say: 'May Allah not forgive you,' and Allah and His angels respond to those two angels: 'Amin.'"

Then, according to al-Tahawi, it is obligatory once in a lifetime, and according to al-Karkhi, it is obligatory every time his name is mentioned. The latter is the precautionary view, and it is the view of the majority. As for sending blessings upon others in a subordinate manner, such as saying, "May Allah bless the Prophet and his family," there is no dispute about it. But if one singles out others from the Family of the House with blessings, that is disliked, and it is one of the distinctive practices of the Rawafid (Rafidites).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verse 57:

﴿Indeed, those who cause harm to Allah and His Messenger﴾ — i.e., they cause harm to the Messenger of Allah. The name of Allah is mentioned for honour (al-tashrif). Or, the expression "causing harm to Allah and His Messenger" is used metaphorically (majazan) to denote doing what does not please Allah and His Messenger, such as disbelief (al-kufr) and denial of prophethood (inkar al-nubuwwah). It was made a metaphor in these two cases — whereas the literal sense of harm (haqiqat al-idha') can be conceived with regard to the Messenger of Allah — so that metaphor and literal meaning would not be combined in a single word.

﴿Allah has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter﴾ — Allah has expelled them from His mercy in both abodes.

﴿And He has prepared for them a humiliating punishment﴾ — in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verse 58:

﴿Those who harm the believing men and believing women without their having earned it﴾, he states the harm to Allah and His Messenger in absolute terms, and restricts the harm to the believing men and believing women, because that (harm to Allah and His Messenger) is never without right, whereas this (harm to the believers) may be rightful, such as the hadd (prescribed punishment) and the ta'zir (discretionary punishment), and it may be wrongful. It was said: it was revealed concerning some hypocrites who used to harm ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, and would say things to him directly. And it was said: it was revealed concerning fornicators who used to follow women while they were unwilling. And from al-Fudayl: "It is not lawful for you to harm a dog or a pig (p-45) without right, so how about harming believing men and believing women?!" ﴿Then they have borne﴾, they have taken upon themselves,

﴿a slander﴾, a great lie,

﴿and a manifest sin﴾, clear.

"O Prophet, tell your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers to draw their outer garments close around them." "Al-jilbab" (the outer garment, a large cloak covering the whole body) is that which covers everything, like the milhafa (wrap), according to al-Mubarrad. The meaning of "yudnina 'alayhinna min jalabibihinna" is that they should let them down over themselves and cover with them their faces and their sides. It is said: if a woman's garment slips from her face, "adni thawbaka 'ala wajhika" (draw your garment over your face). The "min" here is for partitiveness (*li-l-tab'id*), meaning that they let down part of their jilbab, and its excess, over their faces, veiling themselves so that they are distinguished from the slave-woman. Or the intended meaning is that they should wrap themselves in some of the jalabib they possess, and that a woman should not go about in a shift and a head-covering (*khimar*) in the manner of a slave-woman, when she has two jalabib or more in her house. This is because women at the beginning of Islam were, as was their habit (*hijjirahunna*) in the Jahiliyya, going about unveiled in negligent dress: a woman would emerge in a shift and a head-covering, with no distinction between the free woman and the slave-woman. When they went out at night to attend to their needs among the palm groves and the fields, the young men would accost the slave-women, and at times they would accost the free woman, supposing her to be a slave-woman. So they were commanded to differ in their dress from the dress of the slave-women, by wearing wraps and covering the heads and faces, so that no one who desires them would covet them. This is His saying: ﴿That is more suitable that they will be known and not be harmed﴾, meaning: it is more fitting and more worthy that they be recognized and so not be molested.

﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving﴾, for what has passed of their negligence,

﴿Merciful﴾, in teaching them the etiquette of noble conduct.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verse 60:

﴿If the hypocrites do not desist, and those in whose hearts is a disease﴾, "fujur" (immorality), and they are the fornicators, from His saying: ﴿so that one in whose heart is a disease might covet﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 32]. ﴿And the agitators in the city﴾: they are people who used to spread bad news about the expeditions (sarayā) of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), saying: "They were defeated, and they were killed, and such-and-such happened to them," thereby breaking the hearts of the believers. It is said "arjafa bi-kadha" when one reports something not in accordance with reality, because it is an unsettled, unstable report, from "al-rajfah," which is the quaking (al-zalzalah).

﴿We will surely set you upon them﴾, i.e., We will command you to fight them, or We will empower you over them.

﴿Then they will not remain as your neighbours therein﴾, in the city. This is conjoined ('atf) to "la-nughriyannaka," because it is permissible for the oath to be answered by it, given the correctness of your saying: "If they do not desist, they will not remain as your neighbours."

Since exile from the homeland was greater than all that they had suffered, He conjoined with "thumma" (then), because its state is distant from the state of what it is conjoined to.

﴿except for a little﴾, a little time. The meaning: "If the hypocrites do not desist from their enmity and their plotting, and the wicked from their immorality, and the agitators from what they fabricate of bad news, We will surely command you to do the deeds that displease them, then to compel them to seek exile from the city, and to not dwell with you in it except for a little time, until they depart." That is called ighra' (incitement, al-tahrish) in a metaphorical sense.

(Mal'ūnīn) is in the accusative, either as a term of reproach (shatm) or as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), meaning: "They shall not dwell near you except as cursed." Hence the exception (istithnā') applies to both the adverbial of place and the circumstantial clause together, as was mentioned earlier. It cannot be governed by "ukhidhū", because what follows the conditional particle (kalimat al-sharṭ) does not govern what precedes it.

(Aynamā thuqifū) means: wherever they are found.

(Ukhidhū wa-qutṭilū taqtīlā) — the doubling in qutṭilū indicates intensification (al-takthīr).

Sunnata Allah (﴿Sunnata Allāh﴾), in the position of an emphatic verbal noun, meaning: Allah has established regarding those who are hypocritical toward the prophets that they shall be killed wherever they are found,

﴿fī alladhīna khalaw﴾, meaning: those who passed away,

﴿min qablu wa-lan tajida li-sunnati Allāhi tabdīlan﴾, meaning: Allah does not change His sunnah, rather He applies it in one uniform manner among the nations.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verse 63:

﴿They ask you, the people, about the Hour.﴾ The polytheists would ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the time of the establishment of the Hour, out of haste and as a form of mockery. The Jews would ask him as a test, because Allah (Exalted is He) had concealed its time in the Torah and in every Book. So He commanded His Messenger to answer them that it is a knowledge which Allah has reserved for Himself. Then He made clear to His Messenger that it is near at hand, as a threat to those who were hasty and as a calming of those who were testing him, by His saying: ﴿Say: Its knowledge is only with Allah. And what would make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near.﴾ (p-47) Something near; or because the Hour carries the meaning of "al-zaman" (time).
Qur'an 33:64: "Indeed, Allah has cursed the disbelievers and prepared for them a blaze (sa'ir)," meaning a fire of intense blazing.

Concerning ﴿Abiding therein forever﴾: this refutes the doctrine of the Jahmiyyah (a sect that held that Paradise and Hell will eventually perish), since they claim that Paradise and the Fire will come to an end. There is no pause (waqf) at "سَعِيرًا" (saʿīran, "a blazing fire"), because His words "خالِدِينَ فِيها" (khālidīna fīhā, "abiding therein") are a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) referring back to the pronoun in "لَهُمْ" (lahum, "for them").

﴿They will find no protector or helper﴾: "نَصِيرًا" (naṣīran) means a helper who would prevent them (from punishment).

Mention.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verse 66:

﴿On the Day their faces are turned over in the Fire﴾: they are turned about in all directions, as you see a piece of meat turning in the cooking pot when it boils. The faces are singled out because the face is the most honoured part of a human being's body. Or the face may stand for the whole person.

﴿They will say﴾: here ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ is a *ḥāl* (circumstantial clause, describing the state in which the action occurs).

﴿Oh, would that we had obeyed God and obeyed the Messenger!﴾ So that we might be freed from this punishment. They wish for this when wishing no longer benefits them.

﴿And they say: "Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our chiefs (sādatanā)"﴾: the plural of sayyid (master, chief), with the reading "sādātinā" (in the plural of plural, jam' al-jam') attributed to Shami, Sahl and Ya'qub. The intended meaning is the chiefs of disbelief who instructed them in disbelief and made it attractive to them.

﴿"and our elders (kubarā'anā)"﴾: those advanced in years among us, or our scholars.

﴿"and they led us astray from the way (fa-aḍallūnā al-sabīlā)"﴾: it is said "ḍalla al-sabīl" (he went astray from the way) and "aḍallahu iyyāhu" (he led him astray from it). The addition of the alif (in al-sabīlā) serves to lengthen the voice (iṭlāq al-ṣawt). The verse-endings (fawāṣil al-āy) were made like the rhymes (qawāfī) of poetry. Their benefit is the pause (waqf), and the indication that speech has ended and that what follows is a new sentence (mustaʼnaf).

**"Our Lord, give them double the punishment of the Fire"** (for their going astray and their leading others astray),

**"and curse them with a great curse"**. Ibn Kathir... [no]

Here is the translation:

**﴿Our Lord, give them double the punishment⁠﻿﻿﻿...﴾**

Let me restate cleanly:

**"Our Lord, give them double the punishment from the torment"** (for going astray and leading astray),

**"and curse them with a great curse"**: with the letter bā' (ب) ʿĀṣim read it (لَعْنًا كَبِيرًا with the bā'), to indicate the most intense and greatest cursing; and others read it with the thā' (ث), to multiply the number of those cursing. It was revealed concerning Zayd and Zaynab, and what was said about it by some people.

(p-48) ﴿O you who have believed, do not be like those who abused Moses, but Allah cleared him of what they said.﴾ "Ma" is either a verbal-noun particle (maṣdariyyah) or a relative pronoun (mawṣūlah). Whichever it is, what is meant is his being cleared of the content of the saying and its implication, namely the defect-laden matter. The harm done to Moses (peace be upon him) was the story of the prostitute whom Qarun sent to slander him by claiming he had lain with her, or their accusation that he had killed Harun. Allah (Exalted) then brought Harun back to life, and he informed them of Moses' innocence, just as Allah cleared our Prophet (ﷺ) by saying: ﴿Muhammad is not the father of any man among you﴾ [al-Ahzab: 40]. ﴿And he was honourable (wajīhan) in the sight of Allah﴾: that is, of standing, rank and high position, one whose supplication is answered. Ibn Mas'ud and al-A'mash read: "wa-kāna ʿabdan li-llāhi wajīhan" (and he was a servant of Allah, honourable).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verse 70:

﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and speak words of appropriate justice.﴾ (Truthful and correct, or aiming at the truth.) And "al-sadad" (correctness, rectitude): aiming at the truth and speaking with justice. The intent is to forbid them from what they were engaged in regarding the story of Zaynab, without aiming at and speaking with justice; and the exhortation is that they should make their speech correct in every matter, because guarding the tongue and the correctness of speech are the head of all good. Do not pause at "sadidan" (appropriate), because the response of the command is His saying:

﴿He will set right your deeds for you﴾: he will accept your acts of obedience, or he will grant you success in doing righteous deeds.

﴿And forgive you your sins﴾: that is, he will wipe them out. The meaning is: be mindful of God in guarding your tongues and in making your speech upright. If you do this, He will give you what is the ultimate aim of seeking: the acceptance of your good deeds and reward for them, and the forgiveness of your evil deeds and their expiation. This verse confirms the one before it. That verse was built on the prohibition of what harms the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and this one is built on the command to fear God in guarding the tongue, so that the prohibition and the command follow one another. The prohibition is followed by what contains a warning, namely the story of Moses (peace be upon him), and the command is followed by an eloquent promise. Thus this strengthens what turns one away from harm and what calls one to abandon it. When He linked the great success to obedience with His words, ﴿And whoever obeys God and His Messenger has indeed achieved a great success﴾, He followed it with His words:

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verse 72:

﴿Indeed, We offered the trust (al-amanah) to the heavens and the earth and the mountains﴾, and by "the trust" he means obedience to God, and by "bearing the trust" he means betrayal. It is said: "So-and-so bears the trust (hamil li-l-amanah) and carries it (muhtamil laha)," meaning: he does not deliver it to its owner until it leaves his custody (dhimmah), since the trust is as if it were riding upon the one entrusted with it, while he is its bearer. For this reason it is said: "Debts have ridden him (rakibat-hu al-duyun)," and "I have a right over him (li alayhi haqq)." So when he discharges it, it no longer rides him, nor is he its bearer. The meaning is that these great bodies, the heavens, the earth and the mountains, submitted to God's command with the submission befitting their kind, which is what is possible for inanimate things (al-jamadat), and they obeyed Him with the obedience that befits them, in that they did not resist His will and His desire, in bringing into existence, forming, and arranging them in various forms and diverse shapes, as He said: ﴿Then He turned to the heaven when it was smoke, and said to it and to the earth: "Come, willingly or unwillingly." They said: "We come willingly."﴾ [Fussilat: 11]. He also informed us that the sun, the moon, the stars, the mountains, the trees and the beasts prostrate to God, and that among stones there are those that fall down out of fear of God. As for man, his condition in what is valid from him of obedience, and what befits him of submission to God's commands and prohibitions, is not like the condition of those inanimate things in what is valid from them and befitting them of submission and non-resistance, though he is a rational animal, fit for moral responsibility (taklif). This is the meaning of His words: ﴿so they refused to bear it﴾, that is, they refused to commit betrayal in it and to fail to deliver it,

﴿and they were afraid of it﴾, and feared betrayal in it,

﴿but man bore it﴾, that is, he betrayed it and refused to deliver it,

﴿Indeed, he was a wrongdoer, ignorant﴾, because he abandoned the discharge of the trust,

﴿ignorant﴾ (jahul), for failing to recognize what would make him happy, although he was able to attain it, which is its discharge. Al-Zajjaj said: the disbeliever and the hypocrite bore the trust, that is, they betrayed it and did not obey, whereas those among the prophets and the believers who obeyed are not described as "wrongdoing, ignorant." It has also been said: the meaning of the verse is that what man was charged with is so great that it was offered to the greatest and strongest of the bodies God created, and they refused to bear it and feared it, and man bore it, despite his weakness. Indeed, he was a wrongdoer, ignorant, in that he bore the trust and then did not fulfil it, and took it upon himself and then betrayed what he had undertaken. Expressions of this kind are numerous in the language of the Arabs, and the Qur'an came only in their styles. Among that is their saying: "If it were said to fat, where are you going? It would say: I am straightening the crookedness."

(p-50) The *lam* in ﴿that Allah may punish the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women, and the polytheist men and the polytheist women﴾ is the *lam* of purpose (*ta'lil*, expressing cause or reason), because punishment here is equivalent to discipline in your saying, "I struck him for discipline." So do not stop at "ignorant."

﴿And Allah turns in mercy to the believing men and the believing women.﴾ Al-A'mash read "wa-yatubu Allah" with a *raf'* (nominative vowel), making the purpose apply only to the action of the one who bore the trust, and beginning a new clause with "wa-yatubu Allah." The meaning of the well-known reading is: "that Allah may punish the bearer of the trust, and turn in mercy to others who did not bear it." This is because if repentance is accepted from the faithful, it is a kind of punishment for the treacherous. Or the *lam* indicates outcome, meaning: "Man bore it, so the matter ended in the punishment of the wretched and the acceptance of the repentance of the blessed."

﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving﴾ to those who repent,

﴿Merciful﴾ to His believing servants.
